judge_notes.opus5: Item 0 is the CFO on the record that holding Section 301 rates means 'we may have some upside to our earnings outlook' with gross exposure down from ~$200m to ~$75m and no new apparel action since 24 July; item 3 is the broad public series (Census clothing stores +4.5% for the quarter and +5.0% in September, the month management said carries most of Q3) pointing the same way, and item 2 is a short that doubled to 18.6% of shares out while the stock fell 26% with no company news. The brake is item 5: a first full-quarter call under a new CEO after a September rebrand is exactly the shape of the February guide that cost -20.3%.
judge_notes.opus55: The CFO's on-record tariff upside to guidance, cash at ~55% of market cap, and a short base that doubled (i0-i2) against the risk that the new CEO resets 2027 investment (i5).
judge_notes.sonnet55: CFO-flagged tariff upside to the guide and cash-rich washed-out stock with a built short, partly offset by Q3 gross-margin and new-CEO reset risk.
judge_notes.fable51: CFO flagged tariff upside to the outlook with rates unchanged since, $654M of cash at 55% of market cap, a short that doubled into a 26% fall, and September apparel sales +5%; the new-CEO investment reset is the risk.
